extracted.intended_audience: researchers, dataset builders, annotators, and image-generation engineers constructing visually grounded math-problem datasets (GSM8K-V style)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for extracting mathematical information from word problems and producing multi-scene, visually faithful images that encode only the information needed to solve the final question. Covers triple representation, scene allocation, rendering strategies, interference, image-generation rules, and human verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue must not provide numeric values
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue involves characters communicating contextually relevant text in speech bubbles. The dialogue should never directly provide numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: “A customer says ‘I’d like a large pizza’”, “A teacher says ‘Let’s start the exam’”. Use speech-only for semantic content when numbers must be withheld from dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triple representation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a math word problem, identify only the mathematical information required to solve the final question, and represent it as triples: (object, math value, semantic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRIPLE DEFINITIONS: object = the entity described (product, character, item, tool, vehicle). math value = the associated numeric attribute (integer, decimal, ratio, unit). semantic = the contextual role of this fact (placement, relation, or action). Output in the specified JSON format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete math information classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete math information: Object is a countable, physical entity and math value is a pure integer (no units/decimals/percentages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ("apple", 3, "in the basket"). Use this classification when the object is countable and the value is an integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract math information classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract math information: Object is abstract (time, distance, price, weight, score, duration) OR math value is not an integer (e.g., 1.5, 20%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ("distance", "12 miles", "between A and B"). Treat such facts differently during rendering (textual/meta descriptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rendering strategy for small vs large vs abstract values
rubrics_metrics.description: How to render different numeric types: small countable values (<=10) shown visually; large integers (>10) decomposed; abstract values expressed textually or via meta-descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small countable values (<=10): Render directly as visual elements (visual_detail). Large integers (>10): Decompose into m = a [op] b with a <= 10; show 'a' visually, 'b' via speech bubble or text. Abstract values: express textually or with meta-descriptions (e.g., sign board for prices, calendar for dates, ratio graph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene allocation and grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Group triples into scenes based on context so related facts appear in the same scene; the final scene contains only the target question (no numeric values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group facts that are contextually related into the same scene. The final scene should use final_scene_description and omit numeric values so the question remains non-numeric visually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference types (controlled interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional insertion of distractors to increase difficulty: perception interference (visual but irrelevant objects) and semantic interference (semantically close distractors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perception example: extra decorative items in a shop scene. Semantic example: show apples and pears when only apples are required. Use interference sparingly to preserve solvability.

rubrics_metrics.name: JSON output schema requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured JSON output must follow the specified schema with scenes array, each scene having scene_id, interfere, and scene_math_information entries containing raw_math_information, object, math_value, semantic, use_strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed interfere values: "none" | "perception" | "semantic". Use_strategy options include Distance, Object Measurement, Weight, Graph Ratio, Cross Scene Clock, Dashboard, Day, Sign Board, Action, Visual Detail, Speech Bubble, Label. Follow exact field names and hierarchical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance meta-description composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Distance meta description should render an object as a road sign board with two distinct real-world location icons and a double-headed horizontal arrow between them representing distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition: Two location icons horizontally aligned on opposite sides; arrow spans between them with midpoint-centered label, bold and unobstructed; icons and label must be clear and centered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object measurement meta-description composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Object measurement meta description: render a single concrete object with a dimension line (bold double-headed arrow) showing the numeric label at the midpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition: Object centered with space around it; arrow aligns with relevant edges (length/width/height); arrow tips flush with boundaries; numeric label centered and legible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight meta-description composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Weight meta description: place the concrete object on a digital scale whose screen shows the weight as the exact math value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Object centered on weighing surface; display at front and angled to viewer; numeric weight shown in black digits, clearly visible with no glare or obstruction; no overlaps or extra labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph ratio meta-description composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Graph ratio meta description: represent ratios as a pie chart divided into T equal radial segments where T = sum of counts, with a legend below mapping colors to semantics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start division at top center and proceed clockwise. Legend: horizontal items with small colored square then text ‘[semantic]’. Place pie chart at semantic position; ensure all objects visible and not overlapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-scene clock meta-description and time rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross Scene Clock: render wall clock with specified time; apply time rule: if > 12:00 subtract 12:00 (e.g., 15:00 -> 3:00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clock appearance: light beige face, dark blue border, black tick marks, bold numerals 1–12, distinct black hour & minute hands. Place clock at indicated semantic position (e.g., upper right).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashboard meta-description composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Dashboard (speedometer-style) render: perfect circle, no needle, with scale 0–NUMA, increment NUMB, every NUMC labeled, ticks evenly spaced and unit label centered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers in black sans-serif font near ticks; label: bold unit (e.g., MPH) centered at bottom; place dashboard at semantic position; maintain even spacing and legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Day (calendar) meta-description composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Day meta description: render a wall-mounted monthly calendar with a colored header and a 7-column grid labeled S M T W T F S, showing days 1–31 as bold numerals in a consistent grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Header example: month name in all caps centered in bold black sans-serif on bright colored header. Grid: 5 full rows of square date cells; ensure consistent column widths and row heights; calendar placed per semantic field content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign board strategy composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign board: render a semantic board that converts the object into a corresponding icon followed by the math value; icon should be on a separate line above the math value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: price list where 'apple' icon appears above '$3'. Ensure textual label (e.g., 'price list') and that each price appears on its own line for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action strategy (visual–textual linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Action links visual-detail and textual-information detail by using clear visual cues that identify which visual elements correspond to which textual math facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved link strategies: 1) Pointing Gesture, 2) Gaze Direction (eyes aligned to referenced object, directed and specific), 3) Torso Orientation toward target, 4) Holding or Touching the relevant object. Use holding/touching only when unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual detail strategy for countable objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Render countable objects as '[math value] [object]' with distinct visual features placed evenly, fully visible, non-overlapping, and easily countable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects should exhibit slight variation in position/size/orientation to enhance perceptual clarity and be arranged so counting is trivial and occlusion is avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech bubble strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Speech bubble must come from a character and state the semantic content, with the character facing forward or slightly angled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speech bubble connected to speaking character with a visible tail, must not overlap other objects, and must fully and exactly state the semantic field content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label strategy for numeric tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels must state the exact math value and be attached to the object's surface or be part of the object's inherent surface marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The object labeled must match the 'object' field content; the label text must exactly match the 'math value' field content and be legible and unobstructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict image-generation sequencing and uniqueness rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Image generation must produce exactly one image per scene, in the exact given order from Scene 1 to Scene N, without skipping, repeating, or regenerating scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not generate multiple images for the same scene or skip any scene. Maintain one-to-one correspondence between scenes and images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image style and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All images must follow a specified Pixar-style rendering: clear, sharp, naturally lit, with consistent character design and background tone; square format exactly 1024 x 1024 pixels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbidden: warm tints, soft color haze, textures, yellow glow. Every image must strictly match all numeric and descriptive details from its corresponding scene, and maintain consistency across scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit textual progress outputs in generation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Before and after each scene generation, the generator must emit explicit status strings announcing generation start, scene description, and completion messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example required strings: 'Now generating Scene 1 image (Pixar-style, at exactly 1024 x 1024 pixels (square, 1:1)).' After finishing: 'Scene x image finished, now generate Scene x+1 image (Pixar-style, at exactly 1024 x 1024 pixels (square, 1:1)).' After all scenes: 'All finished!'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled interference use-case and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: When using controlled interference, label the scene's 'interfere' field appropriately as 'semantic' or 'perception' and ensure the interference preserves solvability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantic interference inserts semantically close distractors (e.g., eraser, pencil when only crayons matter). Perception interference adds visually salient but irrelevant items (e.g., a backpack). Scenes with interference should still allow solving without external assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual human cross-check verification (3C principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each problem is independently validated by two annotators who verify scene fidelity under the 3C principles: Consistency, Completeness, and Compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators also solve each problem to confirm correctness of the derived answer. Items violating 3C are refined or re-rendered; severe violations trigger re-rendering with modified scene descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotator instructions and annotation labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotators are automatically assigned questions in random order, must review question/images, solve the problem (human solution), and choose one annotation label: Correct, Incorrect, or Skip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If choosing Incorrect or Skip, annotators must add a comment (reasons). The training emphasizes consistent use of the supplied error taxonomy. Annotator composition and a one-hour training session are part of the verification protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3C principles defined for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification is guided by: Consistency (preserve entities, quantities, constraints), Completeness (ensure all problem-relevant information is visually available), Compliance (meet safety and formatting standards, avoid sensitive content, ensure legible numerals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items failing any of these principles should be refined; in severe cases, scenes are re-rendered with modified descriptions. Annotators must use the 3C principles when deciding labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of approved meta-description strategies for abstract values
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract values must be rendered via the approved meta-description strategies (Distance, Object Measurement, Weight, Graph Ratio, Cross Scene Clock, Dashboard, Day, Sign Board) rather than raw count visuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the strategy appropriate to the semantic type and follow that strategy's composition and appearance constraints to maintain clarity and solveability.
